title: Cross-site request forgery token, origin and fetch-metadata enforcement
attackSurface: State-changing browser requests carrying a signed double-submit CSRF token

references.id: Cross-Site Request Forgery Prevention Cheat Sheet

hostile.title: Cross-site fetch metadata
hostile.why: A cross-site browser request is rejected before token comparison

hostile.title: Unapproved origin
hostile.why: A credentialed form post from another origin must not pass

hostile.title: Null origin
hostile.why: Null browser origins are not trusted application origins

hostile.title: Missing double-submit cookie
hostile.why: A submitted token is meaningless without its matching signed cookie

hostile.title: Cookie and token mismatch
hostile.why: Two independently valid tokens must still match exactly

hostile.title: Forged token suffix
hostile.why: A tampered token must fail signature and canonical encoding checks

hostile.title: Expired token replay
hostile.why: A captured token remains invalid after its lifetime

hostile.title: Session mismatch
hostile.why: A token issued for one session cannot authorize another session

benign.title: Valid header token POST
benign.why: Ordinary state-changing request with a matching header token and cookie

benign.title: Valid JSON body token
benign.why: JSON-style integrations can carry the token in the request body

benign.title: Valid form body token
benign.why: Classic form posts carry the token in the encoded form field

benign.title: No fetch metadata header
benign.why: Older browsers may omit Fetch Metadata while still sending a valid origin

benign.title: Same-site fetch metadata
benign.why: The default policy permits same-site browser navigation

benign.title: Referer fallback
benign.why: A browser may omit Origin but send a same-origin Referer

benign.title: Valid PATCH request
benign.why: PATCH is state changing and uses the same token rules

benign.title: Masked token submission
benign.why: Masked tokens unmask to the cookie token and resist compression-oracle reuse
